title: a/an and the
subtitle: a sandwich / the sandwich
summary: Use a/an the first time you mention something, and the when it is clear to the listener which thing or person you mean.

lesson.heading: First time, then after that
lesson.text: Joe is telling you about his lunch: *'I had **a sandwich** and **an apple** for lunch. **The sandwich** wasn't very good, but **the apple** was nice.'* He says a sandwich and an apple because it is the first time he talks about them. Then he says the sandwich and the apple because now we know which ones he means.

examples.text: **A man** and **a woman** were sitting opposite me. **The man** was American, but I think **the woman** was British.
When we were on holiday, we stayed at **a hotel**. Sometimes we ate at **the hotel** and sometimes we went to **a restaurant**.

left.label: a/an - not a specific one
examples: Tim sat down on **a chair**. (maybe one of many chairs in the room)
Do you have **a car**? (not a specific car)

right.label: the - a specific one
examples: Tim sat down on **the chair** nearest the door. (a specific chair)
I cleaned **the car** yesterday. (= my car)

lesson.heading: Saying what kind of thing
lesson.text: We use **a/an** when we say what kind of thing or person we mean, and **the** when we point to one specific thing.

examples.text: We stayed at **a very cheap hotel**.
**The hotel** where we stayed was very cheap.

lesson.heading: When it is clear which one we mean
lesson.text: We use **the** when it is clear from the situation which thing or person we mean. In a room, for example, we talk about **the light / the floor / the ceiling / the door / the carpet**.

examples.text: Can you turn off **the light**, please?
I took a taxi to **the station**.
(in a shop) I'd like to speak to **the manager**, please.

left.label: the + place we all know
left.text: We say (go to) the bank / the post office / the doctor / the dentist - the speaker is usually thinking of a specific one.
examples: I have to go to **the bank** and then I'm going to **the post office**.
Clare isn't well. She's gone to **the doctor**.
I don't like going to **the dentist**.

right.label: a/an - one of many, or a job

lesson.heading: once a week, £1.50 a kilo
lesson.text: We use **a/an** to mean 'each' or 'per' in expressions of frequency, price and speed.

examples.text: I go to the cinema about **once a month**.
'How much are those potatoes?' '**£1.50 a kilo**.'
Helen works eight hours **a day**, six days **a week**.

lesson.text: Before you say *the*, ask yourself: does the listener already know which one I mean? If not, use *a/an*.

exercises.explanation: It is the first time the accident is mentioned, and accident begins with a vowel sound: an accident.

exercises.prompt: This morning I bought a book and a magazine. ___ book is in my bag, but I can't remember where I put the magazine.
exercises.explanation: The book has already been mentioned, so now we know which book: the book.
Can you close the door, please? It is clear which door we mean - the one in this room.

exercises.prompt: This house is very nice. Does it have ___ garden?
exercises.explanation: We don't know yet whether there is a garden, so it is not a specific one: a garden.

exercises.prompt: I like living in this house, but it's a shame that ___ garden is so small.
exercises.explanation: It is clear which garden we mean - the garden of this house.

exercises.prompt: A car crashed into a tree. ___ of the car wasn't hurt, but the car was badly damaged.
exercises.explanation: The car has already been mentioned, so its driver is a specific person: the driver.

exercises.prompt: We had dinner in ___ best restaurant in town.
exercises.explanation: There is only one best restaurant in town, so we use the.

exercises.prompt: There isn't ___ airport near where I live.
exercises.explanation: Not a specific airport, and airport begins with a vowel sound: an airport.
There is only one nearest airport, so it is specific: the nearest airport.

exercises.prompt: I go to the cinema about once ___ month.
exercises.explanation: In expressions of frequency, a/an means 'each': once a month.

exercises.prompt: Match the two halves of each sentence.

Helen works eight hours a day,
In a shop you can say: I'd like to speak to

exercises.prompt: Which word is missing in each sentence: a/an or the?

items.text: I have to go to ___ bank today.
I don't like going to ___ dentist.
We stayed at ___ very cheap hotel.
___ hotel where we stayed was very cheap.
